title: Borel quotients and Borel characters under a multiplicative isogeny
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $X^*(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(G,\mathbf G_m)$ for the abelian group of characters, with addition given by multiplication of values, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_G$-modules, with tensor product as addition; zero is the class of $\mathcal O_G$, and an invertible module is an $\mathcal O_G$-module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_G$. A multiplicative isogeny is a homomorphism $f:G\to H$ for which $F[H]\to F[G]$ is faithfully flat and whose scheme-theoretic kernel is finite and diagonalizable. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. Finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. Diagonalizable means isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, where $F[M]$ has basis $e^m$, multiplication $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$, comultiplication $e^m\mapsto e^m\otimes e^m$, counit $e^m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e^m\mapsto e^{-m}$. Let $f:G_1\to G_0$ be a multiplicative isogeny between smooth connected groups and let $N=\ker f$. A Borel subgroup means a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup; solvable means that its iterated derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial, where the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. For every Borel subgroup $B_0\subseteq G_0$, its scheme-theoretic inverse image $B_1=f^{-1}(B_0)$ is a Borel subgroup of $G_1$. The induced map of quotient schemes $$\bar f:G_1/B_1\longrightarrow G_0/B_0$$ is an isomorphism, sending the coset of $g$ to the coset of $f(g)$. The restriction $f_B:B_1\to B_0$ is faithfully flat with kernel $N$, and the following sequence of abelian groups is exact: $$0\longrightarrow X^*(B_0)\xrightarrow{f_B^*}X^*(B_1)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_N}X^*(N)\longrightarrow0.$$ Exactness here includes injectivity of the first map and surjectivity of the last map. Both quotients mean the fppf sheafification of right cosets, where fppf coverings are jointly surjective flat finitely presented maps of $F$-schemes.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, printed p.391: inverse-image Borel, flag-quotient isomorphism and the middle exact row of the displayed diagram, specialized to finite diagonalizable kernel.

proof.text: The kernel $N$ is stable under conjugation, since $f(gng^{-1})=1$ on every test algebra. Conjugation is an action of the smooth connected group $G_1$ by automorphisms of the diagonalizable group $N$. By [lem-sfb-connected-action-multiplicative-type-rigidity] it is trivial. Hence $N$ is central scheme-theoretically. Apply [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-lifting] to choose a Borel $B\subseteq G_1$ with $h=f|_B:B\to B_0$ faithfully flat and finitely presented. Every $n\in N(A)$ centralizes $B$ after every extension of $A$, so [lem-sfb-borel-scheme-normalizer] gives $n\in B(A)$. Thus $N\subseteq B$, without replacing $N$ by its reduced subgroup.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, p.391, inverse-image Borel assertion, expanded using Corollary 12.38, p.244; Proposition 17.20, pp.357--358; Theorem 17.48, p.367.

proof.text: We now identify $B$ with the full inverse image $B_1$. The inclusion $B\subseteq B_1$ follows from $f(B)\subseteq B_0$. If $g\in B_1(A)$, lift $f(g)\in B_0(A)$ locally along the fppf cover $h:B\to B_0$, using base change of coverings [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. On that cover choose $b$ with $f(b)=f(g)$; then $gb^{-1}\in N\subseteq B$, whence $g\in B$ locally. The local maps to $B$ agree because $B\hookrightarrow G_1$ is a monomorphism, and descend by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Their composites with $B\hookrightarrow G_1$ equal $g$ by the same uniqueness. Thus $B_1=B$ on all test algebras. It is a Borel, and $f_B=h$ is faithfully flat with kernel $N$ by the defining fibre product of the kernel.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, p.391: inverse-image Borel; sheaf-local lift calculation. Descent is Stacks descent.tex, Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], the fppf quotients $Q_i=G_i/B_i$ are represented by schemes. The formula $gB_1\mapsto f(g)B_0$ is well-defined. We may lift a section of $Q_0$ locally to $y\in G_0$, and then lift $y$ locally to $g\in G_1$. For this second lift, [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] applied to $f$ gives a faithfully flat finitely presented factor $G_1\to I$ and a closed immersion $I\to G_0$. Its defining ideal is the kernel of $F[G_0]\to F[G_1]$, which is zero since that map is faithfully flat; hence $I=G_0$. The local class $gB_1$ is independent of choices: if $f(g)B_0=f(g\prime)B_0$, then $f(g^{-1}g\prime)\in B_0$ and so $g^{-1}g\prime\in B_1$. The sheaf condition glues these classes to a natural inverse $Q_0\to Q_1$. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], these mutually inverse sheaf maps give mutually inverse scheme morphisms. This proves precisely the stated quotient isomorphism.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, p.391: G/B isomorphic to G\prime/B\prime; quotient universal property of Chapter 5, especially Theorem 5.39 and Corollary 5.27.

proof.text: We prove left exactness using [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal] for $f_B$. If $\chi_0\circ f_B$ is trivial, uniqueness of descent gives $\chi_0=0$, proving injectivity. A character pulled back from $B_0$ is trivial on $N$. Conversely, if $\chi_1:B_1\to\mathbf G_m$ restricts trivially to $N$ as a scheme morphism, the cited universal property gives a unique character $\chi_0:B_0\to\mathbf G_m$ with $\chi_1=\chi_0\circ f_B$. These implications give exactness at $X^*(B_1)$ and at $X^*(B_0)$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, p.391: left and middle exactness of the character row; quotient property of Chapter 5.

proof.text: For surjectivity onto $X^*(N)$, use [lem-sfb-lie-kolchin-triangular-embedding] to embed the smooth connected solvable group $B_1$ into an upper triangular matrix group. The derived series in the hypothesis is a finite subnormal series with commutative quotients, so it satisfies that lemma's solvability convention. By [lem-sfb-triangular-diagonal-kernel], its diagonal homomorphism $d:B_1\to D$ has unipotent kernel $V$ and a diagonalizable quotient $D$ that is smooth and connected. Put $K=N\cap V$. It is unipotent: the inclusion into the unitriangular group restricts to a closed immersion of $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial] to $K\to N$; this inclusion must be trivial. Thus $K=1$ as a subgroup scheme, even for nonreduced $N$. Consequently $d|_N:N\to D$ is injective on every test algebra and is a closed immersion by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-monomorphism-closed-immersion].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, p.391: right exactness of the character row; Theorem 16.30 and Proposition 16.2, pp.324--325,334--335; Corollary 14.18(a), p.284.

proof.text: The closed-immersion clause of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], over the algebraically closed field $F$, applies to $d|_N:N\hookrightarrow D$ and gives a surjection $X^*(D)\to X^*(N)$. Given $\eta\in X^*(N)$, choose $\widetilde\eta\in X^*(D)$ restricting to $\eta$. Then $\chi=\widetilde\eta\circ d\in X^*(B_1)$ has $\chi|_N=\eta$. This proves surjectivity of the required restriction, and together with step 4 finishes the short exact character sequence.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18, p.391: final surjection in the character row; Theorems 12.8--12.9, pp.232--234.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 18.18, proof and middle exact row, printed p.391, with the supporting results in Chapters 5,12,14,16,17 explicitly cited in the steps.
